newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco's Andina to exploit high-grade deposit.
newsitem.headline: Codelco's Andina to exploit high-grade deposit.

text.p: Chilean state copper company Codelco's Andina division is planning to exploit a small high-grade copper deposit to make up for lower grades in sections of its open-cast pit, said a division spokesman.
The deposit, known as La Union, is one of 10 sites at the Andean mine with over 50 million tonnes of copper reserves with average ore grades of 1.7 percent.
The division had planned to start developing La Union this year but has postponed the project until 1999 as grades at the pit have been higher than expected, he said.
Although La Union is tiny compared with the rest of the mine, it will make it easier to maintain production despite falling grades, he said.
"The advantage of La Union is that it gives flexibility in the way we exploit areas with lower grades," he told Reuters.
La Union will be exploited as an open-cast pit and is expected to produce 30,000 tonnes of fine copper between 1999 and 2003.
Andina, Codelco's third largest division, mined 154,000 tonnes of copper last year. Production will rise to 250,000 tonnes a year in 1999 when its current expansion plan is completed.
Codelco is studying new projects at Andina which could include a further production hike at the mine, which lies 100 kilometers north of Santiago, he said.
"We are thinking of new projects which probably include a future expansion," he said.
"We won't necessarily wait for the (current) expansion to be completed before embarking on other projects."
